task.title: Creating an action log
task.shortdesc: To verify that Red Hat Quay is forwarding action logs to Splunk, you can create a robot account in an organization and search the Splunk index for the forwarded JSON log entries.

ul.li: You have installed Splunk and created a username.
You have generated a Splunk bearer token.
You have configured your Red Hat Quay config.yaml file to enable Splunk.

step.cmd: Log in to your Red Hat Quay deployment.
Click on the name of the organization that you use to create an action log for Splunk.
In the navigation pane, click Robot Accounts → Create Robot Account.
When prompted, enter a name for the robot account, for example splunkrobotaccount, then click Create robot account.
On your browser, open the Splunk UI.
In the search bar, enter the name of your index, for example, <splunk_log_index_name> and press Enter.

info.p: The search results populate on the Splunk UI. Logs are forwarded in JSON format. A response might look similar to the following:

dlentry.dd: Specifies the type of log event. In this example, authentication indicates that the log entry relates to an authentication event.
Specifies the user account involved in the event.
Specifies the individual who performed the action.
Specifies the repository associated with the event.
Specifies the IP address from which the action was performed.
Specifies additional metadata related to the event, when present.
Specifies the timestamp of when the event occurred.
